# Scoring audit: CPU cost reduced; dependable ARC parity not achieved

The reviewed implementation is integrated as experimental opt-in code. Defaults remain continuous, synchronous, stride 1, flat scoring. Astra accepts the implementation and considers this bounded investigation complete, with explicit limitations. It does **not** approve a claim that every optimization is exhausted, that throughput reliably matches ARC, or that semantic ranking provides a serving/capacity benefit.

The clearest gain is lower background CPU consumption: readiness plus executor CPU fell from about **17.9 to 5.2 ms per scoring job**, approximately **71%**. The final serving comparison nevertheless failed: throughput was **2.71% and 2.27% below ARC**, and median release-to-first-token latency was **12.81% and 12.22% worse**.

## What changed

- Removed the ordinary request-completion path's global scoring-queue wait. Empty completion polls and completion of an unrelated request no longer force all score futures to finish. A completed source's final query survives under its original bounded lease; abort/reset invalidate it.
- Enabled bounded asynchronous opportunity scoring using the existing controller. It projects only required immutable summary fields, rejects a full queue before scanning the bank, charges conservative method/batch/dtype-dependent tensor workspace, and uses one executor for one scoring stream.
- Carried request START generations, scheduler/reset epochs, DRAM residency versions, original expiry and opportunity leases through final consumption. Duplicated/reordered/stale observations fail closed. Query and async expiry use the original stricter deadline, rather than refreshing an old feature.
- Reduced capture work with owned slice/concatenation selection, reentry-safe layout consumption, cached operator identity, no-callback dispatch bypass, continuous empty-bank gating and guarded debug formatting. Opportunity snapshots remain available when the current DRAM bank is empty because a later tool-wait decision can still need the final query.
- Suppressed repeated identical idle-status JSON records while retaining metadata and operational transitions.
- Added fixed 500-microsecond cooperative event query/sleep waits for outstanding async work and score completion before the existing readback. This reduces active host waiting. It adds no pinned-buffer pool or independent background service, and preserves completion/lifetime fences. OS scheduling can delay a result beyond one interval.
- Corrected optional profiler endpoint accounting and kept aggregate measurements active during tracing. Supported-layout guards and configuration defaults remain intact.

All six production modules match the independently reviewed source pins exactly. Two test files use package-qualified helper imports for normal repository collection; this changes no test behavior. See [integration receipt](INTEGRATION.json).

## What the measurements mean

The earlier long query-selection timer mostly contained a synchronization boundary: the CPU waited while previously launched model kernels ran, and could not launch subsequent attention. Replacing selection alone moved that wait to readback. Deferring scoring safely removed the launch obstruction; it did not eliminate the underlying model work.

The corrected historical 12-step trace shows capture wall time **22.17 → 3.96 ms**, with **17.01 ms** of capture-side synchronization absent from the candidate. Actual CUDA activity supports overlap in that bounded window. These are diagnostic host envelopes, not final-source whole-run savings or exclusive GPU arithmetic.

The later real-model continuous-scoring diagnostic measured the background CPU reduction:

| Phase | Earlier CPU per measured job | Final CPU per job | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Input readiness | 11.186 ms | 0.567 ms | −94.9% |
| Executor, excluding readiness | 6.699 ms | 4.653 ms | −30.5% |
| Readback, already inside executor | 5.732 ms | 3.630 ms | −36.7% |
| Readiness + executor | 17.885 ms | 5.221 ms | −70.8% |

Only readiness and executor are disjoint here; adding readback again double-counts. The reference aggregates cover 1,013 of 1,030 jobs, while final aggregates cover all 1,028. Natural histories and optional profiler endpoints differ, so this is not an identical-history causal comparison. Controlled tiny reversed tests independently confirm the wait mechanism's CPU benefit with about 0.26–0.34 ms added wall latency.

Queue-wait mean increased **1.74 → 2.34 ms**. Full-queue drops were **11 → 12**; final published feature age averaged **27.8 ms**, with a **683 ms** maximum, all within the original 1,000 ms lease. Final pending jobs/bytes/events were zero. Readback still consumes **3.73 s CPU** in the diagnostic; its remaining driver/copy/observer contribution is unresolved. Sleeping removes CPU spinning, not GPU work or all background cost.

One correlated full KV D2H copied 2.25 MiB in about **42 microseconds**. Its enclosing first-summary host span was about **52 ms**, with only about **0.069 ms** of correlated summary kernels. Host submission, first-use and observer costs prevent interpreting the enclosing span as DMA or removable compute. No observed summary/D2H overlap justified deleting source-block lifetime fences.

## Final serving result and anomalies

Final frozen order was ARC → candidate → candidate → ARC. Both products used the same cached Qwen3-4B dense model, BF16/TP1/eager runtime, 640 GPU KV blocks (1,440 MiB), 448 MiB DRAM, threshold 2 and ARC retention. Each completed the same 45-request simulated six-agent/12-background workload and 3,264 output tokens. Detailed source/runtime profiling was off; common compact validation hooks and product logging remained.

| Pair | ARC tokens/s | Candidate tokens/s | Throughput change | Median first-token change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| First | 82.366 | 80.135 | −2.709% | +12.814% |
| Reversed | 82.087 | 80.222 | −2.272% | +12.217% |

The predeclared screen required both throughput estimates within 1% of ARC and selected first-token summaries no more than 5% worse. **Both final pairs fail.** Mean first-token latency was nearly unchanged and background means improved slightly; that does not erase the throughput/median failures.

The agents are closed-loop: one request's completion plus its private tool wait determines the next release. Exact submitted content/output therefore does not guarantee identical cache work, batches or final completion tail. Final candidates executed 77,747 prompt tokens versus ARC's 80,499, but a different agent finished last about a second later. Less total work can coexist with a longer critical tail. The data do not establish a unique cause of that divergence.

Crucially, final products submitted **zero asynchronous score jobs and zero constrained ranking decisions**. They exercised real query capture, opportunity bookkeeping and actual prefetch transfers, but all-fit/single-source cases bypassed ranking. Thus the new wait code did not execute in those products; blaming it for the regression is unsupported. The failed final-source screen remains valid negative evidence nonetheless.

An earlier repaired revision passed two pairs at +0.31%/+0.40%; the first revision had a mixed passing/failing block. All are retained. Choosing the favorable block would hide instability rather than establish dependable ARC parity. The continuous diagnostic exercises real scoring; the native CPU integration exercises two genuinely competing sources and exact prefix selection. Neither substitutes for an organic competitive-serving benchmark.

Other corrected anomalies include GPU annotation tails being counted as host steps, missing executor aggregates while tracing, and short-scope CPU endpoints including observer bookkeeping after wall sampling. Inclusive host/CUDA envelopes remain nonadditive; startup-inclusive allocator peaks and sampled occupancy are not VRAM savings.

## Verification and acceptance limits

- **367 native CPU tests** with CUDA initialization forbidden, including real scheduler/ARC/metadata/worker construction through constrained opportunity selection, stale/duplicate transport, unequal TTL, budget and reset/cancellation cases.
- Tiny real CUDA tests for exact scores/ties across three methods, owned BF16-to-float32 query snapshots, delayed readers, actual outstanding work at injected failure, retained references/charge through the cleanup fence and exact recovery.
- **225 final requests, 16,320 output tokens and 30,345 recomputed ordered native key recurrences** passed. Observed transfer, staging, readiness/splice/fence and cleanup checks passed. This is retained native execution evidence, not a new independent hardware reproduction by Astra.
- Mac checks passed source-pin identity, syntax, cooperative wait/controller/profiler CPU smoke and `git diff --check`. The full native suite was not rerun on Mac; pytest is absent there. Models/environments were not installed or rebuilt.
- All consumed prefetches still used transfer plus GPU splice; direct native adoption was zero. There is no demonstrated reduction in fixed KV VRAM, supported concurrency increase, capacity gain or organic semantic-ranking value.
- Qualification is limited to the tested dense TP1/PP1 eager runtime and small demand-generated banks. The runtime is the documented reconstructed source subset plus compatible wheel; cached weights use retained metadata/size provenance rather than a fresh full-content rehash.

Large-bank stack reuse, batching/index/fusion, summary-schema changes and CPU mirrors remain reasonable deferrals. A cooperative pinned-copy alternative is untested and may help residual readback, but adds buffer ownership/accounting risk without a proven marginal serving benefit. Astra considers it unnecessary for this experimental handback. Keep ARC as the performance reference; do not promote this mode by default on current evidence.

## Evidence and cleanup

- [Independent final Astra acceptance](astra-acceptance.md), [initial diagnosis](astra-diagnosis.md), [first rejection](astra-final-review.md), [repaired-source review](astra-round2-review.md).
- [Final native report](round4-results/round4/REPORT.md), [component comparison](round4-results/round4/component-comparison.csv), [per-request comparisons](round4-results/round4/paired-requests.csv), [final source/measurements archive](round4-handback.tar.gz).
- [Earlier repaired revision](round2-results/round2/REPORT.md), [rejected blocking/pinned wait test](round3-results/round3/REPORT.md), [first measured revision](results/scoring_audit/REPORT.md). Negative evidence remains intact.
- [Final native cleanup handoff](round4-cleanup/round4/cleanup_receipts/HANDOFF.md), [Mac validation](MAC-VALIDATION.json), [storage inventory](STORAGE.json), [Windows transfer cleanup](WINDOWS-TRANSFER-CLEANUP.json).

Owned processes, project locks, native custody and obsolete offer waits are released. Models, runtime, reusable caches, shared settings and unrelated work are preserved. No commits or pushes were made. Useful compressed raw results, frozen sources, review reports and rollback files remain outside Git.
